tenant_boundary.derivation: The server derives tenant_id from the authenticated principal and derives environment from the typed route or plan-bound server context. Request bodies, query parameters, headers supplied by an application client, agent output, and model context are never authoritative for either value.
tenant_boundary.immutability: tenant_id and environment are bound into the server request context before authorization and remain immutable through read, proposal, approval, execution, verification, audit, export, and Workspace safe-return projections.
tenant_boundary.deny_rule: A valid object identifier, approval, cursor, session, or capability from another tenant or environment is refused before existence disclosure. There is no cross-tenant fallback, lookup, join, replay, or global default.
tenant_boundary.future_enforcement_gate: No production route may ship until middleware derives the context server-side, every repository query requires it, persistence constraints prevent cross-tenant references, and the cross-tenant denial fixture passes at the API, broker, event, audit, export, and model-context surfaces. Phase 0 proves only the planning contract and fixture assertions.

platform_administration.scope: platform code, intellectual property, tenant provisioning, licensing terms, platform configuration, release governance, and platform-wide security controls
platform_administration.delegation: No customer, tenant administrator, agent, or service identity receives platform ownership or an implicit platform-admin capability.

tenant_administration.launch_scope: Joe administers the single CARR tenant; Dell operates authorized business records and remains Control Room Reporter/Viewer at launch.
tenant_administration.future_scope: An owner-controlled seat license may grant narrow tenant-local capabilities without transferring platform or intellectual-property control.

explicit_exclusions: a shared application database across CARR and future customer tenants
customer ownership or transfer of platform code or intellectual property
tenant_config_allow_list: tenant display name and safe labels
approved workflow-version selection from the platform registry
tenant_config_denies: tenant-supplied code, scripts, SQL, expressions, or command strings
platform policy, risk, audit, retention, redaction, or approval bypass

workflow_governance.definition: Each workflow has an immutable workflow_id, immutable version, owner, tenant, purpose, typed inputs and outputs, risk class, exact resources and environments, executor qualification, approval policy, rollback or compensation, evidence contract, maintenance owner, and retirement path.
workflow_governance.promotion_rule: Promotion is a separately authorized, audited governance decision. Every promotion binds named evidence, one immutable workflow version, one accountable owner, a completed observation window, explicit failure criteria and handling, tested rollback, an adoption result and adoption test, and a cutover plan and cutover gate. A workflow cannot self-promote, skip a state, or treat usage count as approval.

promotion_evidence_envelope.experimental_to_pilot: The accountable owner freezes the immutable workflow version and opens a bounded observation window with named evidence, failure criteria and handling, tested rollback, adoption result and adoption test, and a cutover plan whose cutover gate remains closed.
promotion_evidence_envelope.pilot_to_approved: The accountable owner presents named evidence for the immutable workflow version after its completed observation window, including failure criteria and handling, tested rollback, adoption result and adoption test, and a cutover plan with an explicit approved-or-closed cutover gate.
promotion_evidence_envelope.approved_to_standard: The accountable owner presents named evidence for the immutable workflow version after its completed standard-readiness observation window, including failure criteria and handling, tested rollback, repeated adoption result and adoption test, and the cutover plan whose standard cutover gate has passed.

workflow_governance.execution_rule: A work request and plan pins one workflow version. A later promotion, revision, or retirement never mutates a running plan or revives an expired capability.
workflow_governance.retirement_rule: Retirement blocks new starts, preserves historical evidence and version identity, names the replacement or reason, and defines how active work drains, rolls back, or is re-planned.
locked_rails: audit, evidence, redaction, retention, and approval invariants
registered actuator boundary and no arbitrary code or SQL
flexible_rails: owner-approved workflow steps within typed capabilities
safe labels, views, thresholds, and notification preferences
executor routing among qualified registered executors
workflow version choice within the approved registry
workflow_governance.bounded_trial: An experimental workflow may enter a tenant-local pilot for at most 5 business days with named owner, hypothesis, exact scope, success and stop criteria, rollback, evidence, and automatic expiry. The trial creates no new source of truth, performs no destructive migration, introduces no parallel writer, and is not a generic workflow engine. Expiry cannot promote or continue the workflow; the owner must explicitly retire, revise into a new version, or approve the next lifecycle decision.
workflow_governance.doc_outage_rule: Routine operations remain usable through straightforward typed controls, status, runbooks, and evidence when Doc is unavailable. Doc explains, accepts intake, and routes; Doc is not an authorization boundary or a required control-plane dependency.
workflow_governance.future_enforcement_gate: Phase 0 validates the lifecycle and evidence contract only. Promotion mutation, workflow execution, and retirement enforcement remain absent until council approval, implementation, rehearsal, and independent verification.

maintenance_accounting.target: 3–5 human hours per month for normal internal maintenance
maintenance_accounting.baseline_rule: Measure actual human time; do not estimate or invent a baseline.
exception_categories: tenant onboarding beyond the launch tenant
maintenance_accounting.accounting_rule: Every entry records measured_minutes, category, normal_or_exception, tenant, service or workflow, actor, occurred_at, and evidence_ref. Exception time is reported separately and never used to make the normal target appear met or missed.
maintenance_accounting.toil_trigger: More than 5 measured normal-internal human hours in each of two consecutive calendar months opens a named toil-reduction work request with the largest categories and a bound product action.
maintenance_accounting.mature_claim_gate: A low-toil or mature-maintenance claim requires at least three complete consecutive months of measured entries, separate exception accounting, and evidence that the toil trigger was evaluated.
scorecard: workflow and service concentration of toil
deduplicated actionable alert count and acknowledgement latency
deterministic safe automation success, refusal, and verification rates
open maintenance remedies with owner and due evidence
integrity_rules: No health, security, authority, incident, or audit control may be disabled or suppressed to meet the maintenance target.
No normal work may be mislabeled as an exception and no exception may be hidden from the scorecard.
Alerts deduplicate only when tenant, resource, condition, and evidence window match; each alert remains actionable with owner, severity, source, freshness, and remedy.
A deterministic safe automation is typed, tenant-bound, idempotent, allow-listed, bounded, observable, and complete only after outcome verification; refusal and failure remain visible evidence.
Every breached target or repeated alert binds a named remedy or work request instead of becoming a vanity metric.
maintenance_accounting.future_enforcement_gate: Phase 0 defines fields, tests, and bound actions; it does not claim a measured baseline, elapsed three-month evidence, or live maintenance automation.
